root_cause.text: In the SLIP VJ header decompression path, slhc_uncompress() used decode() and pull16() to parse optional fields without validating the packet buffer against isize, and decode() additionally masked pull16()’s result with `& 0xffff`, making intended `== -1` exhaustion checks unreachable and allowing out-of-bounds reads on short compressed frames.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states “Neither helper bounds-checks against isize, and decode() masks its return with & 0xffff so it can never return the -1 that callers test for -- those error paths are dead code,” and the patch fixes this by changing `decode()`/`pull16()` to take an end pointer, return `-1` on exhaustion, and adding `if (cp + 2 > end) goto bad;` before reading the TCP checksum.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add end-of-buffer context and error-capable return handling to decoding helpers to prevent unsafe or invalid reads.
intent_record.what: The function declarations were changed so that decode() and pull16() now take an additional const unsigned char *end parameter, and pull16()'s return type was changed from unsigned short to long.
intent_record.how: This enables both functions to receive a buffer boundary pointer for validating reads during decoding/parsing, and the widened pull16() return type allows it to propagate non-16-bit status or error values instead of only returning an unsigned data value.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add end-of-buffer checks to decode and 16-bit extraction so truncated input returns -1 instead of reading past the buffer.
intent_record.what: The patch changes pull16() to take an additional end pointer, changes its return type and local variable from unsigned short/short to long, adds a bounds check that returns -1 if fewer than two bytes remain, and updates its comment accordingly. It also changes decode() to take the same end pointer, adds a check that returns -1 if no bytes remain before reading, passes end to pull16(), simplifies the return logic, and updates the comment to document the -1 exhaustion case.
intent_record.how: At runtime, decode paths now verify that the input buffer still contains enough data before consuming bytes, preventing reads past the end of the buffer. When the buffer is exhausted or truncated, decode() and pull16() return -1 as an error signal instead of dereferencing invalid memory, allowing callers to detect incomplete input safely.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add an end-of-buffer pointer in `slhc_uncompress()` to support bounds checks and prevent out-of-bounds packet parsing.
intent_record.what: A new local variable `const unsigned char *end` was added in `slhc_uncompress()`, initialized to `icp + isize`, alongside the existing packet buffer pointer `cp = icp`.
intent_record.how: This introduces an explicit pointer to the end of the input buffer, enabling subsequent bounds checking against the packet size during decompression to avoid reading past the provided input data.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a length check before reading the TCP checksum so truncated compressed packets are rejected safely.
intent_record.what: A new bounds check was added before reading the TCP checksum from the input buffer: if `cp + 2 > end`, execution jumps to the `bad` error path; otherwise the existing `thp->check = *(__sum16 *)cp; cp += 2;` logic runs unchanged.
intent_record.how: This prevents the function from reading two bytes past the end of the compressed packet buffer when extracting the checksum, causing malformed or truncated input to be rejected through the existing error handling instead of triggering an out-of-bounds memory access.

intent_record.intent_summary: Pass the input buffer limit to decode() during TCP header field decompression to enforce bounds checking and prevent over-read errors.
intent_record.what: The calls to decode() inside slhc_uncompress() were changed from decode(&cp) to decode(&cp, end) in four places handling NEW_U, NEW_W, NEW_A, and NEW_S compressed-field updates.
intent_record.how: This makes decode() receive the buffer end pointer while decoding urgent pointer, window, ack, and sequence deltas, allowing it to validate reads against the input boundary and fail with -1 instead of potentially reading past the compressed packet data.

intent_record.intent_summary: Pass the input buffer end pointer to decode when handling NEW_I so decoding is bounded and cannot overrun the packet data.
intent_record.what: The call to decode in the NEW_I branch of slhc_uncompress was changed from decode(&cp) to decode(&cp, end), adding the end pointer as a second argument.
intent_record.how: At runtime, decode can now use the end boundary while parsing compressed packet data, which helps prevent reading past the available input buffer when decoding the NEW_I field and avoids invalid packet processing that would otherwise fall through or corrupt state.
